findings.issue: The blend is never evaluated under the controller's metrics before the iteration is spent. The only local signal produced is per-member LightGBM global AUC; no GAUC or nDCG@5 is computed anywhere in the script, at any weight. The stated hypothesis falsifier is expressed purely in controller terms ("controller primary does not exceed 0.6576323250719152 by the campaign's frozen epsilon"), so the scientific claim is unfalsifiable until the attempt is already consumed, and 0.25/0.75 is shipped untested against 0.0/1.0 (which reproduces attempt 8 exactly, since within-user monotone transforms preserve both metrics).

findings.issue: The two members are nested (attempt-8 features = attempt-7 features + 6), share the same seed, params, split, and refit schedule, so their within-user rank vectors will be strongly correlated and the achievable blend movement may be smaller than the epsilon the falsifier demands. Inter-impression elapsed time is an upper bound on the predecessor's play time (it absorbs idle, scroll, and request latency), so previous_long_view_proxy_code == 2 systematically over-predicts the predecessor's true long_view relative to the documented rule I verified in the README.

findings.issue: Compute roughly doubles the parent attempt (4 booster fits, two full prepare_events passes over 5,055,984 rows, and two feature-matrix builds per frame) with redundant work that is exactly removable. Estimated peak RSS ~2-2.5 GB, which fits, and estimated runtime fits the ~966 s/attempt implied by elapsed_seconds 7730 over 8 attempts, but the redundancy is free to remove if wall clock is tighter than it appears.

strategy_notes: Leakage audit passed on the path that actually matters here. long_view[i] is reconstructible from time[i+1] - time[i] under the same rule the README documents, so a single forward delta would be a hard leak; the code constructs none. previous_gap_ms, previous_duration_ms, session_start, session_position, and all four proxy summaries resolve to row i or strictly earlier rows in the ['user_id','time_ms','__row_order'] timeline, and the recent-window shifts are guarded by session_position > lag.

Output contract is valid and self-checking: predict_from_checkpoint asserts source_order == arange(n) before scoring, validates member prediction shape and finiteness, and np.save writes one float32 per authoritative row. The executability clauses of the falsifier are enforced in code (weight sum at module import and in validate_manifest, consumed != rows in within_user_percentile_ranks, non-finite checks in build_feature_matrix and predict_member), not merely asserted in prose.

Within-user percentile ranking is metric-safe: GAUC and nDCG@5 depend only on within-user ordering, so weight 1.0 on either member would reproduce that member's score exactly. That makes the 0.25/0.75 blend a genuine perturbation of attempt 8 with a clean fallback, and it makes the 'retain attempt 8 if primary misses epsilon' branch of the falsifier coherent.

Evidence citations reconcile with the packet: every EDA figure quoted (0.7422197404, 0.6706248142, 3489/11662) matches research_plan.eda_observations verbatim, the two parents' primaries recompute exactly from their cited GAUC/nDCG@5, and the attempts=8 / best_attempt=8 / scored_iterations=6 state is consistent with the attempt 1-2 failures described. Attempt 1's falsifier (play_time_ms absent from evaluation_features) is respected: neither EVALUATION_REQUIRED nor TRAIN_REQUIRED references that column.

I verified the KuaiRand README independently (https://github.com/chongminggao/KuaiRand/blob/main/README.md); the long_view definition is min(duration_ms, 18000), matching LONG_VIEW_THRESHOLD_MS and the proxy threshold. I did not and could not inspect the attempt 7 or attempt 8 source, so the claim that the first 24 features 'exactly preserve attempt 7' is taken on the packet's word; if that is wrong the blend is still a self-contained valid experiment, just against slightly different members than advertised.
